description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between ACC (%) and Co-occurrence Number for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3, with tick labels at intervals of 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and ranges from 60% to 85%, with tick marks at intervals of 5%. The plot features six distinct lines: the “Base” method is represented by a black line with solid circles; “FT” is a blue line with upward-pointing triangles; “IKE” is a red line with upward-pointing triangles; “MEND” is a brown line with diamond markers; “MEMIT” is a purple line with upward-pointing triangles; and “ROME” is a green line with square markers. All lines show a general upward trend as the Co-occurrence Number increases. The “Base” line starts at approximately 65% ACC at a Co-occurrence Number of 1 and ends at approximately 83% ACC at 10^3. The “FT” line starts at approximately 67% ACC at a Co-occurrence Number of 1 and ends at approximately 82% ACC at 10^3. The “IKE” line starts at approximately 69% ACC at a Co-occurrence Number of 1 and ends at approximately 82% ACC at 10^3. The “MEND” line starts at approximately 72% ACC at a Co-occurrence Number of 1 and ends at approximately 84% ACC at 10^3. The “MEMIT” line starts at approximately 71% ACC at a Co-occurrence Number of 1 and ends at approximately 83% ACC at 10^3. The “ROME” line starts at approximately 76% ACC at a Co-occurrence Number of 1 and ends at approximately 85% ACC at 10^3.
